name: Jason Heflin
fact: Contemporaneous confirmation of his post, and of how it began: the Herald calls him a Russellville senior and co-chairman of the Hillraiser committee, the new SGA committee President Keith Coffman introduced at the first Congress meeting of 1997-98. Heflin said the group would sit together at athletics events and sponsor drawings and contests at football, basketball, baseball, soccer and volleyball games.

name: Matt Bogard
fact: As chairman of SGA's campus improvements committee he co-authored the resolution asking Western to install two emergency telephones in the south campus car park, which Congress passed on 16 February 1999. Campus police captain Mike Wallace disputed the need for them; Bogard said the phones were a necessity because the car park is isolated and badly lit. He is still at Western in August 2004, when the Herald prints a letter from him as a graduate student from Taylorsville.

name: Jeff Baynham
fact: He helped rebuild SGA's web site in 1998, working with Brad Sweatt on a page that would post all legislation Congress passed each week and list officers' e-mail addresses. The Herald calls him a Lexington sophomore.

name: Adam Leach
fact: He was a member of Western's first mock trial team, started in spring 2001 by government professor Margaret Ellis, and is quoted on arguing a case in front of a judge as an undergraduate. The Herald calls him a Princeton senior.

name: LaJohna Brown
fact: She was the resident assistant on the third floor of Bates-Runner Hall in autumn 2001, when construction crews woke her freshmen at six in the morning. The Herald calls her a Nashville sophomore and says she had lived in South Hall her own freshman year.

name: Braden Wilson
fact: He sat on the SGA campus improvements committee that passed the bill of 5 March 2002 allocating $7,000 for new outdoor furniture in front of Cherry Hall, alongside John Bradley, Rick Upchurch and Emily Butler; the older benches were to be repainted rather than scrapped.

name: Terry Woodall
fact: He was named a Spirit Master in December 2003, and the Herald ran the congratulatory advertisement with his portrait in February 2004. In November 2004 he was at the Warren County courthouse on election night with the economics professor Brian Strow, who was standing for the county commission.

name: Troy Ransdell
fact: As a senior political science major from Louisville he wrote a signed commentary in the Herald against Western's proposed plus/minus grading system, arguing that no one had shown how it served students and that grades are not there to reward or punish. He was SGA's chief justice that year.

name: Michelle Woods
fact: She was one of two Western government students who won six-week summer internships in Washington in 2002, hers with the Washington Center's student internship clearing house. The Herald calls her a Hodgenville junior and quotes her saying she would like to be a congresswoman one day.

name: Jenny Stith
fact: She was president of the Alpha Delta Pi chapter by November 1999; the Herald calls her a Rineyville senior in its report on the Mr. Hilltopper pageant, which Alpha Delta Pi sponsored for the Ronald McDonald House. It had called her an Elizabethtown freshman in 1997.

name: Andrea Lovell
fact: She chaired SGA's campus improvements committee in 2000-01. The Herald's end-of-year review of the year in student government carries a pull quote from her, labelled campus improvements committee chairwoman, in which she says the committee set twelve goals a semester and met all of them; the story names her as a Powderly junior. The archive's officer list has her in 2000-01 only as a Congress member inferred from an award nomination.

name: Jodi Clinard-Pulley
fact: She was made a Spirit Master in April 2001, four years after her year on Congress, and the Herald photographed the ceremony. It calls her a senior from Springfield, Tennessee, which places her at Western from about 1997 to 2001.

name: Sally Eilerman
fact: She took over as co-chairwoman of the Hillraisers at the start of 1998-99 and is quoted at length on rebuilding the group, which former SGA president Keith Coffman had revived the year before. The Herald calls her a Fort Thomas junior.

name: Kyle Matthews
fact: He sat on SGA's campus improvements committee, not only academic affairs, and worked members through a proposal asking Western to put sprinkler systems in all dormitories after the Murray State fire of 18 September 1998 killed one student. The Herald calls him a Woodburn freshman and names Laura Hancock as the committee's chairwoman.

name: Larry Murphy
fact: Contemporaneous confirmation of his chairmanship: the Herald names him as the committee chairman for SGA's academic affairs while reporting the committee's work on newsletters and bulletin boards.

name: Jenny Stith
fact: Contemporaneous confirmation of her chairmanship: the Herald calls her SGA's public relations chairwoman and an Elizabethtown sophomore while reporting the committee's work on the skywalk proposal.

name: Michelle Woods
fact: As chair of SGA's academic affairs committee she sponsored the resolution asking Western to inquire into the effectiveness of its Freshman Seminar courses, which passed Congress unanimously on 19 February 2002; she then took it to the Freshman Seminar committee herself.

name: Tim Gilbert
fact: He was crowned Coming Home King in February 2001 as the Alpha Gamma Delta candidate, and was then president of Phi Delta Theta; the Herald calls him an Owensboro junior.

name: Conrad Davies
fact: In April 2000, as a Frankfort sophomore, he walked into the middle of the crowd that had gathered around the travelling evangelist Jim Gilles outside Downing University Center, put a hand on Gilles's shoulder and tried to pray with him. Gilles refused, saying his earrings prevented it.

name: Elizabeth Pemberton
fact: She was house manager of the Phi Mu chapter in 2000-01, which places her at Western from at least 1999 into 2001.

name: Carla Givens
fact: Appears in the Herald in text but never in a photograph. The paper spells her Givens/Givin and confirms the cohort: a news brief headed 'Psychology students win awards' calls her a Dry Ridge sophomore who won first place for best undergraduate psychology paper presentation at the Kentucky Academy of Sciences, 13-15 Nov 1997, and an overall third place for the Richard Griffith Memorial Award. A sophomore in January 1998 fits the Rodes Hall seat she held that year. The item is a text-only brief in the News briefs column; page 14 carries only two halftones, a Super Bowl watch-party crowd and an Army ROTC advertisement, neither of them her. She is nowhere else in the digitised Herald 1993-2005.

name: Julia Raymer
fact: Photographed by the Herald, but the frame carries no usable face. A 'Pet project' picture on the campus page shows her collecting food and litter for the Humane Society in Downing University Center with Greenville freshman Donjea Osborne, both Phi Sigma Pi members; the caption names her and places her at left, so the identification would be secure. The photograph is shot from directly overhead and both subjects are bent over their work, so only the tops of their heads are in frame and no face is visible. She is an Owensboro senior in October 2001, which fits a Congress seat in 1998-99. No other photograph of her appears in the digitised Herald 1993-2005.

name: Adrienne Frey
fact: Photographed by the Herald with a caption that identifies her beyond doubt, but the frame is unusable. Shawn Poynter's night picture 'Fired up' on the campus page shows two students at a bonfire on the DUC south lawn and names them 'Louisville freshmen Kathleen Speicher, left, and Adrienne Frey', so Frey is the right-hand figure. It is a long exposure against the fire: the left subject is a solid silhouette and the right subject is only rim-lit, a bright edge of hair and a sliver of cheek, with no facial features recoverable at 700 dpi. The caption independently confirms her cohort, a Louisville freshman in November 1998, which fits the freshman seat she held that year. This is the only photograph of her in the digitised Herald 1993-2005 and the only appearance of her name in it.

src.label: College Heights Herald 74:20, 10 November 1998, p. 2 (PDF p. 3)

name: Martha Bonds
fact: In the Herald repeatedly in text, never in a photograph, and two of her appearances are the exact trap the poll method has to guard against. Her name and home town are set in bold at the foot of the Opinion page on 18 February 1997 and again on 13 March 1997, which reads like a poll label in OCR, but both are letter-to-the-editor signature blocks: the 18 February block sits in the far right column above 'SEE LETTERS' with no frame anywhere near it, and the 13 March page discusses her letter in two replies while the People Poll on the same page carries five other people. The one story built around her, a feature on the Women in Transition group of 21 October 1997 which calls her a Scottsville senior and the group's president, carries a single large photograph whose caption names Beverly Wimpee, a Bowling Green senior, with her children, not Bonds.

src.label: College Heights Herald 73:16, 21 October 1997, p. 10 (PDF p. 11)

name: Lindsey Sullivan
fact: Photographed by the Herald at an SGA event, with a caption that names her, but the frame gives no face. H. Rick Mach's picture 'Sweepin' up' on the campus page of 22 October 1998 shows Campus Sweep behind Cherry Hall, an event the caption says the Student Government Association co-sponsored with the Herald and Free the Planet, and names 'Sophomore Lindsey Sullivan of Lebanon, Tenn., and Ohio City Josh Hampton'. It is shot from ground level: the foreground is two pairs of legs and a broom head, and the only whole figure is far back across the road, its head about forty halftone dots wide and turned down over the broom, unreadable at 900 dpi. Which of the two named students that figure is cannot be settled either. The caption does confirm her cohort, a sophomore in October 1998, consistent with Congress service in 1997-98 and 1998-99.

src.label: College Heights Herald 74:17, 22 October 1998, p. 2 (PDF p. 3)

name: Bill Brown
fact: Twice in the Herald in the same week of November 1995 and photographed once, but the frame is unusable and the identification would not hold anyway. Alyse Preston's Shantytown picture of 14 November 1995 captions three students, 'Louisville sophomore Chris Snyder (left), laughs with Edmonton sophomore Jennifer Glass and Bill Brown, a freshman from Evansville, Ind.'; only Snyder is given a position, so Glass and Brown are not separable, and the night exposure prints the right-hand figure as solid black with no facial detail recoverable at 600 dpi. His name also sits under a mugshot in the opinion-page poll of 9 November 1995, 'Bill Brown, freshman from Evansville, Ind.', which would be provable, but that is three years before the 1998-99 Congress and Bill Brown is among the commonest names in the paper, so nothing ties the 1995 freshman to the member who spoke against the Kappa Alpha Order funding bill on 1 December 1998.

name: John Tebault
fact: The Herald photographed him alone, with a caption naming only him, and the frame is still not a portrait. Chad Stevens's front-page picture of 17 October 1996, headed 'Seeing double', reads: 'After receiving his resident assistant application from the Residence Life office Tuesday afternoon, Elizabethtown freshman John Tebault makes his way down a hall on the fourth floor of Potter Hall.' It is a backlit art shot of him and his reflection in a dark corridor; at 900 dpi the head is a solid silhouette showing an outline of nose and chin and no features at all. The caption does fix him firmly: an Elizabethtown freshman in October 1996 is a sophomore in 1997-98, which is the Sophomore Off-Campus seat the archive records, and a junior in 1998-99. He stayed at Western and by 2003 was the Herald's own advertising manager, which is why his name recurs in the staff box on the opinion page from 2000 onward and not in any further news photograph.
